method: Editorial target-fit screen of all 66 group entries, followed by scoped historical evidence checks for accepted edges. Discovery shortlists are not a completed review of their journals or a ranking.
policy: Principal means an important selected venue, not uniquely most important. No minimum or maximum quota.
Require sustained historical or institutional role; current remit, title match, founding year and one isolated famous article are insufficient.
Edge intervals delimit the reviewed role, not the field’s lifespan. 2000 is a coverage boundary.
Full text, extracts, abstracts and participant retrospectives retain distinct access/attribution qualifications.
A missing principal edge is an evidence/target-fit gap, not evidence that a field lacked important journals.
Book series and political/primary-source periodicals do not become research-journal nodes merely to fill a field.

discovery_leads.title: Travaux du Cercle linguistique de Prague

field_reviews.target_fit_and_next_step: Linguistic-school and serial identities need checking; do not equate the entire tradition with one historical research journal.
Distinguish French historical epistemology from general philosophy/history of science.
Earlier professionalization requires period-specific evidence and language coverage.
Distinguish political and primary-source periodicals from later research venues; verify eligibility first.
Check journal-yearbook history and the relation to the Durkheimian school.
Check Weber’s editorial role and the wider remit; do not infer a Weberian journal from authorship alone.
Resolve title changes and German historical-school periodization.
Select only historically relevant programmes; no blanket link from economics journals to this broad intellectual tradition.

discovery_leads.title: Annals of the Association of American Geographers

field_reviews.target_fit_and_next_step: Review historical-geography contributions over time, rather than infer from discipline-wide remit.
Earlier cultural history is not one journal community; verify exact serial forms before considering links.
A later specialist venue cannot stand for the entire earlier biographical/literary tradition.

discovery_leads.title: Journal of the Royal United Service Institution

field_reviews.target_fit_and_next_step: Professional strategic periodicals may be primary sources; distinguish them from historical research venues.
CSSH link covers a bounded historical-method interface; dedicated candidates still need longitudinal histories.
National traditions require multiple languages and journal communities; avoid assigning one generalist venue to all national narratives.
Add US and cliometric venues after dated institutional/content review; resolve predecessor titles.
Reconcile Military Affairs and earlier titles before applying long intervals to the modern title.
Different political-historical approaches need different evidence; generalist remit alone is insufficient.
Review the historical life-writing strand; avoid treating all literary autobiography research as historical scholarship.
1929 founding edge retained. Reconcile ESC, HSS and wartime title records before accepting a multi-decade principal edge; generic Annales is ambiguous.
NLR is accepted for a qualified historical role; fuller P&P/labour-venue comparisons remain leads.
Retain the original-title founding edge; do not backdate the African American History title or assume uniform journal politics.
Distinguish anticolonial intellectual periodicals from research journals; add African-language and regional evidence rather than infer from titles.
Three principal venues selected; broaden languages and national traditions before calling the shortlist representative.

discovery_leads.title: Comparative Studies in Society and History

field_reviews.target_fit_and_next_step: Publication of modernization debates does not show journal endorsement or a single modernization school.
Four venues selected; labour history and non-Anglophone journals still need comparison.
The atlas entry is an umbrella; do not fabricate a single identity-history journal community.
OHR selection is US-weighted; British and other-language traditions are explicit next comparisons.
Current selections cover interdisciplinary historical social science; review dedicated methods and cliometric venues separately.
Cambridge School is narrower than intellectual history. Skinner’s 1969 publication alone does not make the whole journal a school venue.
Resolve exact Review identity; compare world-systems and Latin American dependency rather than equate them.
P&P cultural strand selected; sustained historical roles of interdisciplinary theory journals require further review.
Distinguish philosophical/literary journals from venues for historical arguments; review dated contributions.
Italian microhistory and German everyday history require separate journal histories; original regional title is not the later Quaderni title.
Three society-title intervals selected. Environment and History remains a later international candidate, with no restored founding claim.
Subaltern Studies is a book series; do not manufacture a journal node. One connected-history article does not establish a principal school venue.

discovery_leads.title: Signs: Journal of Women in Culture and Society

field_reviews.target_fit_and_next_step: Gender History link covers gender history; racial-formation approaches and other journals require distinct evidence.

discovery_leads.title: Journal of the History of Sexuality

field_reviews.target_fit_and_next_step: Separate sexuality history from all queer theory; the 20-year journal retrospective is a lead, not yet a full-text check.
Late launches and broad theory remits need pre-2000 historical-contribution evidence.
A memory special issue is a lead; sustained field role and Holocaust/general-memory distinctions need review.
World History selection has partial-access retrospective evidence. Journal of Global History begins beyond the atlas cutoff and cannot fill this interval.
Review Indigenous editorial agency, methods and regional diversity; journals studying Indigenous peoples are not automatically decolonizing venues.
Psychoanalytic research periodicals and their use by historians need separate relationships and title checks.

discovery_leads.title: The British Journal for the History of Science

field_reviews.target_fit_and_next_step: Isis selected; compare other national and methodological communities rather than treat one journal as the whole field.

discovery_leads.title: Studies in History and Philosophy of Science Part A

field_reviews.target_fit_and_next_step: The Bloor–Latour exchange is accepted; sustained SSK role and Science Studies predecessor identity remain separate reviews.
Separate STS from SSK; reconcile newsletter/current-title history and read sustained contribution evidence.
Distinguish philosophical concept-history publishing from Koselleck’s historical project; lexicons are not journals.
Check Psychohistory Review identity and avoid equating distinct psychoanalytic schools.
Earlier philosophical traditions span books and later reception; no forced common journal.
Principal link is deliberately broad; distinguish specific debates when better contribution-level evidence is available.

discovery_leads.title: Studies in Philosophy and Social Science

This target is US-specific. RHR newsletter/title history must be resolved; do not substitute British NLR.
Principal and founding roles are distinct; professionalization and movement/journal differences are retained.

limitations: Initial principal selections cover 19 of 66 entries, not a completed worldwide survey.
Evidence access favours English-language journals and publisher/society retrospectives. Non-Anglophone and African-based journals require explicit follow-up.
Annales generic/current/ESC title identities need reconciliation before extending the 1929 founding edge into a long principal interval.
No new historical field nodes or frontend rendering are included.
